name: Helix Corp Standard-Issue Office Day Set
description: The quintessential Tier 3 cubicle uniform, issued or subsidized by Helix Corp and barely distinguishable from the one worn by the person in the next pod over. A medium-grey poly-synth button-down with subtle herringbone texture sits tucked into straight-cut charcoal trousers made from Helix's in-house 'DuraWeave' blend — stiff enough to hold a crease for a full shift, uncomfortable enough to remind you this time belongs to the company. The shirt collar features a discrete BCI port loop sewn into the left placket, sized for standard 3mm neural jacks. Black synthetic-leather belt with a brushed-nickel buckle embossed with the Helix logo. Footwear is the Helix-sourced Cordis Autofit Dress Oxford in matte black — practical, auto-lacing, and entirely forgettable. A laminated ID lanyard in corporate teal hangs at chest height, clipped to the second button. Everything fits adequately. Nothing fits well.
functionality: BCI port loop at collar for standard 3mm jacks, auto-lace footwear for fast floor transitions, stain-resistant trouser finish rated for eight-hour desk shifts, ID lanyard with RFID badge clip
what_it_says: You are employed. You are compliant. You are not yet anyone. The uniform is the point — it signals that you belong to the building, not the other way around. Wearing it outside the office is mildly embarrassing. Wearing it slightly wrong is a disciplinary note.
worn_by: junior support staff on their first corporate contract
price_range: Φ 80–Φ 140 (often partially subsidized via payroll deduction)
story_hooks: A character wearing this uniform is mistaken for a Helix employee while investigating a corporate building — the lanyard gets them through three security checkpoints before anyone looks twice.

The uniform's RFID badge clip has been quietly logging location data to a Helix server for months; a character discovers the firmware and realizes every employee in the building is being tracked to the minute.
A Tier 3 worker shows up to an important meeting in this outfit and is turned away at the executive floor — the elevator literally won't accept their badge above Level 14.

physical_description.visual_profile: The uniform silhouette of corporate compliance—a grey button-down tucked into charcoal trousers, presenting a vertically neutral column interrupted only by a teal ID lanyard at the chest. The impression is one of deliberate uniformity: anonymous, standardized, designed to be forgotten the moment you clock out.
physical_description.fit: Straight-cut and deliberately adequate rather than flattering. The shirt drapes with geometric precision, the trousers maintain rigid geometry front and back. Everything sits at regulation distance from the body—close enough to signal 'professional,' distant enough to feel like borrowed cloth.
physical_description.primary_material: Medium-grey poly-synth for the shirt; Helix DuraWeave (proprietary poly-blend composite) for the trousers. Both are engineered for durability and crease retention over comfort. The belt is black synthetic leather with a brushed-nickel buckle.
physical_description.texture: The shirt carries a subtle herringbone weave—visible but not tactile. The trousers have a faint crosshatch from the DuraWeave blend, creating micro-ridges that catch fluorescent light. Both fabrics are treated for stain resistance and reduced wrinkle recovery, giving them a faintly plastic hand-feel.
physical_description.color_scheme: Medium grey (shirt) over charcoal (trousers), anchored by matte black synth-leather shoes and belt. The teal laminated ID lanyard provides the only chromatic break—a visual tether to corporate identity. Brushed-nickel buckle catches overhead lights.
physical_description.closures: Standard button placket on the shirt; the description notes a discrete BCI port loop sewn into the left placket for standard 3mm neural jacks. Trousers feature a conventional zippered fly and button waist. Shoes are auto-lacing with magnetic snap-closure. ID lanyard clips to the second shirt button.
distinctive_features: BCI port loop integration in left shirt placket (neural jack compatible, 3mm standard)
Helix Corp logo embossed on brushed-nickel belt buckle
Laminated corporate teal ID lanyard with standard clip attachment
DuraWeave trousers engineered for crease retention and stain resistance
Cordis Autofit Dress Oxfords with auto-lacing and matte finish
Herringbone texture on shirt (subtle, almost invisible)
Regulation button spacing and collar width—nothing to distinguish the wearer
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 corporate-subsidized. The quality is adequate and standardized; nothing suggests individuality, expense, or access to black-market customization. This is the uniform of the working-class office pod.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this outfit signals: employed by a mid-tier corpo (Helix), bound to a pod and shift schedule, compliant with neural interface standards, and either willing or resigned to anonymity. It reads as 'middle management adjacent' or 'system administrator'—functionally important, socially invisible.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on day one; broken-in and slightly limp by week two. The creases fade, the synth-leather belt develops micro-scuffs, the ID lanyard corners curl. By month three, the shirt collar shows faint wear at the BCI port loop from repeated neural jack insertion. Nothing is visibly damaged—Helix QA ensures durability—but the outfit quietly documents time served.
